🇷🇺🇺🇸 Global buyers of Russian fuel push back against US sanctions bill, Politico reports

Politico reports that the global reaction to the Russia sanctions bill just approved by Congress was fast and sharp:

Moscow warned the bill will only prolong the war against Ukraine. India vowed to defend its own interests. Beijing pushed back against what it called illegal "extended jurisdiction."

The bill, which still needs Trump's signature, mandates sanctions on Russia's leadership, energy sector, defense industry, and the shipping network moving embargoed Russian fuel. It also hands Trump the authority to impose 100% tariffs on the five largest global buyers of that fuel — a provision already worrying Washington's own allies.

Since 2022: China has bought 50% of Russian oil exports, India 37%, Turkey 5%, the EU 5%. The EU has also been the top buyer of Russian LNG (49%) and the top buyer of Russian pipeline gas (32%) over that period.

On the EU side, critics of the bill argue it hands Trump far too much discretion — either to carve out exemptions for major Russia partners like China, with whom Washington wants expanded trade, or, conversely, to run a vendetta against US allies he doesn't like, such as the EU, using individual member states' oil and gas purchases (Slovakia, Hungary) as pretext.
